Lloyd's best linear unbiased estimators of location and scale

Source: R/os_linear.R
os_blue.Rd

For a location-scale family with standard member \(Z\), the order statistics at the ranks of mom satisfy \(X_{(r_i)} = \mu + \sigma Z_{(r_i)}\), with \(E[Z_{(r_i)}] = \alpha_i\) and \(\mathrm{Cov}(Z_{(r_i)}, Z_{(r_j)}) = B_{ij}\). Lloyd's estimators are the generalized least squares estimators of \((\mu, \sigma)\) in this linear model: \(\hat\mu = \bm w_\mu'\bm X\) and \(\hat\sigma = \bm w_\sigma'\bm X\) with the weights of the Details. They are unbiased and have the smallest variance among linear unbiased estimators from these ranks.

Usage

os_blue(mom)

Arguments

mom

An object of class "osmoments" computed with cov = TRUE at two or more ranks. The weights are computed from its standard component, the moments of the standard member, so they do not depend on the location and scale it was computed with.

Value

A list with w_location and w_scale (the weight vectors, named by rank), var_location, var_scale and cov (the variances and the covariance of the two estimators per unit of the squared scale parameter, so that \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu) = \sigma^2 \cdot\) var_location), ranks, n and dist.

Details

With \(\bm\Omega = \bm B^{-1}\), \(a_{11} = \mathbf 1'\bm\Omega\mathbf 1\), \(a_{1\alpha} = \mathbf 1'\bm\Omega\bm\alpha\), \(a_{\alpha\alpha} = \bm\alpha'\bm\Omega\bm\alpha\) and \(\Delta = a_{11} a_{\alpha\alpha} - a_{1\alpha}^2\), $$\bm w_\mu' = (a_{\alpha\alpha}\mathbf 1' - a_{1\alpha}\bm\alpha')\bm\Omega/\Delta, \qquad \bm w_\sigma' = (a_{11}\bm\alpha' - a_{1\alpha}\mathbf 1')\bm\Omega/\Delta,$$ $$\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu) = \sigma^2 a_{\alpha\alpha}/\Delta, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(\hat\sigma) = \sigma^2 a_{11}/\Delta, \qquad \mathrm{Cov}(\hat\mu, \hat\sigma) = -\sigma^2 a_{1\alpha}/\Delta.$$

Computation. The formulas above define the estimators. The function computes them by whitening the design \([\mathbf 1, \bm\alpha]\) with the Cholesky factor of \(\bm B\) and solving the least-squares problem by QR, which keeps its accuracy when \(\mathbf 1\) and \(\bm\alpha\) are nearly collinear, as for two close ranks at a large \(n\), where \(\Delta\) itself loses its digits. It then checks the four unbiasedness conditions, \(\bm w_\mu'\mathbf 1 = 1\), \(\bm w_\mu'\bm\alpha = 0\), \(\bm w_\sigma'\mathbf 1 = 0\) and \(\bm w_\sigma'\bm\alpha = 1\), and warns when one fails by more than \(10^{-6}\).

Conditions. The distribution of mom is treated as the standard member of a location-scale family, which every os_dist() object is by construction; the required moments exist, which os_moments() has checked; at least two distinct ranks are present, so that the design \([\mathbf 1, \bm\alpha]\) has rank two; and \(\bm B\) is positive definite. The scale estimated is the family's scale parameter: the standard deviation for the normal, the scale of the logistic or Gumbel, and the length of the support for the uniform.

References

Lloyd, E. H. (1952). Least-squares estimation of location and scale parameters using order statistics. Biometrika, 39(1-2), 88-95.

See also

os_moments, os_lin_moments

Examples

m <- os_moments(9, ranks = c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9))
b <- os_blue(m)
b$w_location                     # sums to one
#>        r1        r3        r5        r7        r9 
#> 0.1457682 0.2382168 0.2320301 0.2382168 0.1457682 
sqrt(b$var_location)             # SD of the location estimate per unit sigma
#> [1] 0.3375654
